prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Monthly mean ozone by monitoring station (language en).
Grid: 13 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Station" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 8: header "Jul" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Aug" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 10: header "Sep" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 11: header "Oct" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 12: header "Nov" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 13: header "Dec" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 27px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 725px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 724px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [90, 52, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 52] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [98, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 59] · table 719×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [91, 52, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52, 55, 52, 52] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [96, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52] · table 721×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [88, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [90, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56, 51, 51, 56] · table 723×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [100, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [112, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51, 51] · table 725×233px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3A"],"acceptable":["r2A","r1A","r2B","r3B"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"December is 59px while every other month is 51px; the lone wide final column creates an arbitrary asymmetry that draws the eye away from the data and implies a distinction that does not exist."},{"design":"r1C","why":"May, July and October are 55px while the other months are 52px; the periodic widening creates a false visual grouping and breaks the even rhythm needed to compare twelve equivalent months."},{"design":"r2C","why":"March, June, September and December are 56px while the rest are 51px; the every-third-month emphasis is semantically meaningless and makes the numeric grid look irregular."}],"contrast":{"widths":[190,44,44,44,44,44,44,44,44,44,44,44,44],"why":"The station column consumes nearly a third of the table while each month gets only 44px—below the 49px minimum for a 28px value plus padding—so numbers crowd the borders or wrap, and the eye is pulled to empty space in the row-header column instead of across the monthly series."},"ranges":[[88,100],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52],[50,52]],"rationale":"This is a lookup-and-compare table: twelve equivalent monthly columns should share one width so the eye can sweep across a station's year without rhythmic interruptions. At 52px each month has 31px of text space for 27–28px values, enough to keep every number on one line with a little breathing room. The station column needs more width than the months because 'Station' and names like 'Riverside' are 65px unbreakable, but 100px is enough to establish row-header hierarchy without letting the label column dominate. r3A uses the full 725px measure exactly and keeps all twelve months identical, which is why it edges out the otherwise close r2A and r1A.","principles":{"general":["Columns that play the same role—especially repeated numeric measures—should normally share a width; unequal widths should encode a real grouping or priority.","Set each column's minimum from its longest unbreakable content plus padding, then spend remaining width where it improves scanning rather than distributing it arbitrarily.","A row-header column should be visibly wider than data columns but not so wide that it becomes the table's dominant feature.","Avoid lone wider columns at the end or periodic wider columns unless the content genuinely differs; readers infer structure from width."],"specific":["The twelve months are equivalent measures, so 52px each is the right rhythm; the 3–5px variations in r1C and r2C read as accidental noise.","With 725px and thirteen columns, the budget is tight: months can only range roughly 50–52px before the total exceeds the measure, while the station column can range about 88–100px.","An 88px station column leaves only 2px of slack around the 65px header and names, so it is usable but visibly tighter than the rest of the table."]},"tradeoffs":"A designer could reasonably prefer r2A's 96px station column for a slightly more generous label-to-data ratio, or r3A's 100px for maximum label comfort and an exact 725px fill; the difference is small. One could also argue r2B's 88px station column is acceptable because it still fits, even though it looks cramped.","uncertain":"Whether the 3–4px month-width differences in r1C and r2C are noticeable enough to count as faults rather than harmless variation, and whether a 112px station column (r3B) crosses from generous into disproportionate."}
